title: Vanishing of the left base-change term of the Jacobi-Zariski sequence
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings such that $H_1(L_{B/A})=0$ and the module of Kähler differentials $\Omega_{B/A}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] is a projective $B$-module, where $\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}=\bigl(N_1\xrightarrow{\ \delta\ }N_0\bigr)$, $N_1=I/I^2$, $N_0=\bigoplus_{b\in B}B\,\mathrm d[b]$, is the naive cotangent complex of the canonical presentation $A[B]\to B$ and $H_1(L_{B/A})=\ker\delta$, as in [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. Let $\mathfrak a\subseteq B$ be an ideal and $C=B/\mathfrak a$, and let $\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}\otimes_BC$ be the two-term complex $N_1\otimes_BC\xrightarrow{\ \delta\otimes\mathrm{id}_C\ }N_0\otimes_BC$. Then $$H_1(\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}\otimes_BC)=\ker(\delta\otimes\mathrm{id}_C)\cong H_1(L_{B/A})\otimes_BC=0.$$ More precisely, the map $H_1(L_{B/A})\otimes_BC\to N_1\otimes_BC$ induced by the inclusion $\ker\delta\subseteq N_1$ is injective with image $\ker(\delta\otimes\mathrm{id}_C)$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00S2 (lemma-exact-sequence-NL), final assertion ('if Tor_1^B(Omega_{B/A},C) = Tor_2^B(Omega_{B/A},C) = 0 then H_1(NL_{B/A} (x)_B C) = H_1(L_{B/A}) (x)_B C') and its proof, lines 35444-35446 and 35467-35485; here the Tor hypotheses are replaced by projectivity of Omega_{B/A}, which implies them

proof.text: Write $M=\operatorname{im}\delta\subseteq N_0$. By [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], $N_0$ is the free $B$-module on the symbols $\mathrm d[b]$ and $H_1(L_{B/A})=\ker\delta$; by [lem-weil-pbc-naive-cotangent-complex-cokernel-kahler], $\operatorname{coker}\delta\cong\Omega_{B/A}$ via $\pi:\mathrm d[b]\mapsto\mathrm db$. Hence there are two short exact sequences of $B$-modules $$(E_1)\quad 0\to H_1(L_{B/A})\to N_1\xrightarrow{\ \delta'\ }M\to0,\qquad (E_2)\quad 0\to M\xrightarrow{\ \iota\ }N_0\xrightarrow{\ \pi\ }\Omega_{B/A}\to0,$$ with $\delta=\iota\circ\delta'$ ($\delta'$ the corestriction of $\delta$, $\iota$ the inclusion).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00S2 (lemma-exact-sequence-NL), proof of the final assertion, lines 35467-35485; 'NL_{B/A} = (N^{-1} -> N^0) is a two term complex of B-modules with N^0 free and cohomology modules H^0 = Omega_{B/A} and H^{-1} = H_1(L_{B/A}). Write M for the image of the differential'

proof.text: Flatness of the terms. $\Omega_{B/A}$ is projective by hypothesis and $N_0$ is free, so both are flat $B$-modules by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat]. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ses-kernel-flat] to $(E_2)$ (middle and right terms flat) shows that $M$ is flat.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00S2 (lemma-exact-sequence-NL), proof of the final assertion, lines 35467-35485; Stacks uses Tor_1^B(Omega,C) = 0 and Tor_2^B(Omega,C) = Tor_1^B(M,C) = 0 (dimension shift with N^0 free); with Omega projective these vanish because Omega and M are flat, so the flatness statements Lemma Tag 00HM (lemma-flat-ses, line 9071) and the proof of Lemma Tag 051G (line 24332: projective modules are flat) are used in their place

proof.text: Tensoring with $C$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-quotient-tensor-injective] with $N=C$: to $(E_2)$, whose last term $\Omega_{B/A}$ is flat, it shows that $\iota\otimes\mathrm{id}_C:M\otimes_BC\to N_0\otimes_BC$ is injective; to $(E_1)$, whose last term $M$ is flat, it shows that $$0\to H_1(L_{B/A})\otimes_BC\to N_1\otimes_BC\xrightarrow{\ \delta'\otimes\mathrm{id}_C\ }M\otimes_BC\to0$$ is exact.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00S2 (lemma-exact-sequence-NL), proof of the final assertion, lines 35467-35485; the two exact sequences 0 -> M (x) C -> N^0 (x) C -> H^0 (x) C -> 0 and 0 -> H^{-1} (x) C -> N^{-1} (x) C -> M (x) C -> 0, with Lemma Tag 00HL (lemma-flat-tor-zero, line 9037) in place of the Tor vanishing

proof.text: Conclusion. Since $\delta\otimes\mathrm{id}_C=(\iota\otimes\mathrm{id}_C)\circ(\delta'\otimes\mathrm{id}_C)$ and $\iota\otimes\mathrm{id}_C$ is injective, $\ker(\delta\otimes\mathrm{id}_C)=\ker(\delta'\otimes\mathrm{id}_C)$, which by the exact sequence of the previous step is the image of the injective map $H_1(L_{B/A})\otimes_BC\to N_1\otimes_BC$. Thus $H_1(\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}\otimes_BC)\cong H_1(L_{B/A})\otimes_BC$, and this is $0\otimes_BC=0$ because $H_1(L_{B/A})=0$.

lean.statement: theorem jacobiZariski_leftTerm_vanishing (A : Type u) (B : Type v) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Subsingleton (H1Cotangent A B)] [Module.Projective B (KaehlerDifferential A B)] (a : Ideal B) : let P := (Generators.self A B).toExtension let δ := P.cotangentComplex.rTensor (B ⧸ a) let ι := P.h1Cotangentι.rTensor (B ⧸ a) Function.Injective ι ∧ LinearMap.range ι = LinearMap.ker δ ∧ Nonempty ((LinearMap.ker δ) ≃ₗ[B] (H1Cotangent A B ⊗[B] (B ⧸ a))) ∧ Subsingleton (H1Cotangent A B ⊗[B] (B ⧸ a)) ∧ Subsingleton (LinearMap.ker δ)

reviewed_lean.note: A->B any ring map (CommRing A B, Algebra A B); H1(L)=0 as Subsingleton (Algebra.H1Cotangent A B = (Generators.self A B).toExtension.H1Cotangent, abbrev); Omega projective as Module.Projective B (KaehlerDifferential A B); C = B/a; NL = cotangentComplex of canonical presentation Generators.self (N1 = I/I^2, N0 = S (x) Omega[A[B]/A] free on d[b]); delta(x)id_C and (ker delta incl)(x)id_C via rTensor; injective + range = ker + iso + both zero; no extra hypotheses, universes independent, no new definitions
